• Develop analytical and reporting expertise and mechanisms to support development services activities.
Your responsibilities will include:
• Leading on the grid connections function and grid contract workflows
• Managing the application and modification process for the grid connection agreements, liaising with internal teams, technical support, legal, NGESO and TOs as required, ensuring that all prescribed deadlines are achieved and strategic connections objectives are met.
• Managing the grid security payments for the biannual security periods and on acceptance of contracts, liaising with procurement, accounts and external parties as required, ensuring required payments are assessed and challenged as appropriate, and made within prescribed timescales
• Managing the grid connection contracts and provide management information on key contract deliverables, payments and obligations
• Liaising with the development teams to ensure that all contractual obligations are achieved and all payments are made in line with contractual timescales
• Developing grid-specific reporting, systems and guidance at both a portfolio and granular project/issue level to disseminate learnings to empower teams to adopt cost-effective and efficient approaches to the development of grid connections
• Supporting wider business development activity including stakeholder relationship development, costs and connection modelling, benchmarking and development of KPIs, and application of good governance and internal assurance to provide robust and reliable services to development teams
• Applying analytical techniques and tools to grid and industry data to provide more informative outputs to empower the development teams to achieve their business development objectives.
• Maintaining industry knowledge on relevant wider issues and representations; actively contribute to Statkraft’s industry engagement including working groups and consultation responses.
• Contribute to continuous improvement of Statkraft project development activities through lessons learnt processes, knowledge transfer and mentoring of Project Developers
• Undertaking occasional UK and international travel

Qualifications
• Bachelor Degree in related subject
• Experience of managing stakeholders and functions with competing priorities and timescales
• Full knowledge and understanding of Connections Reform is critical
• Experience developing and managing business processes, systems, documentation and reporting
• Experience in utilising and developing analytical tools including Power BI and other data analytical software is desirable but not essential.
• Excellent communication skills in English.

A career with Statkraft is a career filled with purpose – meaning that every employee is not just making a living, they are making a real difference to the planet, our communities, and the future. • An opportunity to work with renewable energy and contribute to a low emission society
• Professional and personal development in an exciting global company
• A working environment characterized by competence, responsibility, innovation and a strong commercial culture
• A diverse workplace with regards to gender, age and cultural background
• Competitive terms of employment and benefit schemes
• Career and learning opportunities at various levels of the organisation
• The chance to grow your career alongside a truly global network of experts, leaders, specialists and graduates from different countries and background
• Hybrid working
Statkraft manages critical infrastructure and services in several countries. The applicant must be eligible for security clearance and authorisation.
Statkraft's vision is to renew the way the world is powered. To navigate the complex journey ahead, we need every voice at the table. We therefore work actively to be a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcome all applicants regardless of background, gender, age, sexual orientation, religious belief, ethnicity, nationality or disability.

As a Manager within our Restructuring team, you will play a pivotal role in delivering restructuring, turnaround, and insolvency solutions. This role demands a seasoned professional with deep technical expertise, commercial acumen, and a proven track record of success in challenging and dynamic environments. Development of less experienced team members will also be a key part of the role.

• Lead and manage a diverse portfolio of restructuring and insolvency assignments across a range of sectors
• Deliver strategic advice and practical solutions to underperforming or distressed businesses
• Oversee formal insolvency processes including administrations (both trading and pre-pack), liquidations, and CVAs
• Evidence an ability to lead corporate transactions including negotiation of commercial terms and sale documentation
• Conduct detailed financial analysis, including cash flow forecasting and recovery planning would be an advantage but not essential
• Develop and implement strategic recovery plans tailored to client needs
• Advise on financial restructuring, distressed M&A and performance improvement
• Engage with banks, investors, legal advisors and other stakeholders to deliver integrated financial solutions
• Collaborate with legal, finance and operational teams to ensure seamless project delivery
• Build and maintain trusted relationships with clients, lenders and other key stakeholders
• Contribute to business development efforts, including proposal writing and market positioning
• Mentor and develop junior team members, fostering a culture of learning and high performance
• Ensure all work complies with relevant legislation, professional standards and internal policies
• Take a lead role in high-impact, complex restructuring engagements, often involving cross-functional teams and senior-level stakeholders

• Degree educated and CII / CPI required. ACA / ACCA or equivalent qualification is advantageous but not required. JIEB obtained or looking to complete the qualification desirable.
• Deep expertise in restructuring, turnaround, and insolvency developed within a professional services or advisory environment
• Significant experience in corporate restructuring preferred
• Strong technical knowledge of UK insolvency legislation and restructuring frameworks
• Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills
• Commercially astute with a proactive, solutions-focused mindset
• Proficient in Microsoft Office and insolvency case management systems (e.g., IPS)
• Capable of managing multiple priorities and leading teams across concurrent projects
• Proven experience of training junior members of staff and a willingness to do so

Our Values
• Straightforward: We provide clear, no-nonsense advice
• Confident: Our guidance is backed by expertise and evidence

We are always striving to improve in all areas - whether it’s our people, our clients, our planet or our governance. Our ongoing success as a business depends on our sustainability and agility in a changing and challenging global landscape.

We believe every individual should have the opportunity to thrive.
Our learning and development programmes enable us to invest in growing our employees’ careers. We aim to empower our team members to each achieve their potential.
We are committed to growing long-term relationships with our clients and supporting them in achieving their objectives. We understand that our clients’ sustainability and success lead to our sustainability and success. We are emotionally invested in our clients right from the beginning.

As the business continues to grow, so do our teams. We’re looking for a dedicated Water Remedials Consultant to join our team and take responsibility for assessing remedial requirements, developing scopes of work, preparing quotations and supporting the delivery of planned and reactive water remedial works.
This is a home-based role, with travel to client sites as required. We are seeking a proactive, reliable and commercially aware individual who is confident working independently while collaborating effectively with clients, engineers and internal teams.

About This Job
Principal Structural Engineer – Bristol
We invite you to bring your talent and passion into play as you take a leading role in delivering and shaping a wide range of interesting projects across the UK and internationally. If you are an experienced structural engineer looking for the opportunity to combine technical leadership, project delivery, client engagement and team development, our Principal Structural Engineer position in Bristol could be a great fit.
A great place to build your career
You’ll join our Industry & Infrastructure Facilities (I&IF) team in Bristol – a growing regional team with a real sense of community and a strong focus on technical excellence.
Our work spans a diverse range of sectors, including rail, aviation, energy, manufacturing, data centres and other critical infrastructure. The variety of our work means there is plenty of opportunity to apply your experience in new ways and develop your expertise.
We work on projects ranging from early feasibility and concept development through to detailed design and construction, often alongside major clients, contractors and multidisciplinary teams. The wider I&IF service line brings together expertise across structures, civils, MEP, sustainability and other specialist areas, with opportunities to collaborate across the UK and internationally.
Why Bristol?
Bristol offers something a little different. We’re a smaller regional team, so there is a genuine sense of community and plenty of opportunity to influence how we work and where we go next.
You’ll be surrounded by technically strong people who are generous with their knowledge and keen to support each other. Whether you want to deepen your technical expertise, develop your project leadership, build client relationships or help others progress their careers, there are people around you who can help.
We also believe work should be enjoyable. Our active Bristol social team organises everything from padel and other sporting activities to pub quizzes and informal social events.
Our new office is in a great location, close to Temple Meads and Bristol city centre, providing a collaborative base for our growing team.
Your role
As a Principal Structural Engineer, you will:
• Lead the structural design and delivery of projects or significant elements of projects.
• Develop and agree structural concepts, design philosophies and technical solutions.
• Apply advanced engineering judgement to technically challenging and complex problems.
• Take responsibility for the technical quality of your work and the work of others.
• Act as a technical lead and trusted adviser to clients, representing Ramboll at project meetings and helping to develop long-term relationships.
• Inspire, support and coach engineers and technicians, helping to develop technical capability within the Bristol team.
• Work collaboratively with architects, contractors and other disciplines to deliver integrated and practical solutions.
• Promote innovative and sustainable approaches to design, including low-carbon solutions, reuse and efficient use of materials.
• Contribute to the continued growth and development of the Bristol I&IF team.
What we’re looking for
For this role, we believe your starting point is:
• Chartered with the IStructE, ICE or an international equivalent.
• Significant experience as a structural engineer, with a strong track record of delivering technically challenging projects.
• A high level of technical competence and sound engineering judgement across steel, concrete and/or timber.
• Experience taking technical responsibility for projects and leading design teams.
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex engineering principles clearly to clients, colleagues and other stakeholders.
• The ability to build strong relationships with clients and collaborators.
• A willingness to share knowledge, coach others and contribute to the development of the wider team.
• A multidisciplinary mindset and an interest in understanding the wider drivers behind a project.
• A passion for finding better, more efficient and more sustainable ways of solving engineering problems.
Experience in rail, aviation, energy, manufacturing, data centres or other critical infrastructure would be valuable, but we don’t expect you to have experience across all of these areas. We are looking for people with strong engineering fundamentals who are interested in applying their skills to new and varied challenges.
Your opportunity to make a difference
This is an opportunity to join a team that is growing and help shape what it becomes.
You’ll have the support of experienced technical specialists across Bristol, the wider UK I&I team and Ramboll’s international network, while having the autonomy to develop your own client relationships, lead projects and contribute to the direction of the local team.
If you’re looking for a Principal role where you can remain close to the engineering, work on genuinely varied projects, develop people and clients, and play an active part in a close-knit regional team, we’d love to hear from you.
Ready to join us?
Please submit your application. Be sure to include all relevant documents including your CV.
We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So, if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.
Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.
Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll
Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll employs more than 18,000 people globally across 35 countries. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, Management Consulting, and Architecture & Landscape. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we help shape the societies of tomorrow.

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. About This Job
About The Team
The Global KYC and Onboarding Squad is improving Wise's KYC and onboarding experience by reducing three things at the same time:
•
Financial crime risk, by making reviews, controls, and decisioning more effective.
•
Operational cost, by automating repeatable work and improving how agents handle complex cases.
•
Customer friction, by making verification clearer, faster, and easier to complete.
Business Onboarding Verification focuses on business customers. Businesses are not simple identity objects: they are legal entities connected to directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorised signatories, employees, documents, registry data, vendor data, ownership structures, risk signals, and market-specific requirements.
That makes KYB one of Wise's most complex verification domains. It is also one of the biggest opportunities to improve customer experience, reduce manual work, improve control quality, and build better risk decisioning.
About The Role
We are hiring a Product Manager to own one of the workstreams within Business Onboarding Verification. Each PM within the team owns a complex product area end to end, from discovery and roadmap through delivery, measurement, and iteration.
These are not generic AI, programme management, or stakeholder coordination roles. You will coordinate complex work, but the core of the job is product ownership: defining the problem, shaping the solution, making trade-offs explicit, setting success metrics, launching safely, and ensuring each change improves KYB as a product.
What You Will Own
•
Own the product roadmap for one BOV workstream, from discovery through launch and iteration.
•

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/aecom2/74400015.description_excerpt:
About This Job
At AECOM one of our key business lines is Bridges and Structures which is currently expanding due to a number of recent high-profile project wins which will be added to our already impressive portfolio. We are looking for ambitious, hardworking, enthusiastic Civil & Structural Engineering graduates who have computational, mathematical and design skills. Candidates will work on a variety of projects from concept design to implementation for clients who operate either locally, nationally or internationally. Those selected will have to be focused on delivery of results to our clients whilst finding enjoyment in technically challenging projects.
As leaders in the sector, our Bridges and Structures teams provide wide challenging opportunities in an ever-evolving industry. Our undisputable global position could give you the chance to work in the design of UK or international projects between our London, Madrid, Italy, United States and the Middle East offices; undertake the assessment and maintenance of the current UK bridge network, or propose renewal structural works for the current UK bridge network. With both international and domestic clients, we are committed to providing quality, innovative and sustainable solutions using the latest technology in civil & structural engineering whilst taking advantage of our integrated range of services by collaborating with other disciplines within AECOM. Excellence, agility, perseverance, communication, forward-thinking and global awareness are some of the skills that our daily work demands from our teams in order to maintain and enhance our relationship with our clients and stakeholders as competition in the market grows harder.
Recent projects include: Edmonton Capital Line Network Arch Bridge, Canada; Jodrell Bank Telescope; Portage Bay, United States; New Alperton Foot and Cycle Bridge; Panama Canal New Arch Bridge, Panama; Civil Assessment Framework Agreement (CAFA); 10 Dock upgrade at Devonport Dockyard; London Bridge Assessment, Tower Bridge Motor Replacement, Blackfriars Bridge Painting and Refurbishment.
Job Responsibilities
Successful candidates will use industry leading computer software while working on a variety of different bridge specific expertise including:
• Structural Design
• Bridge Assessment
• Finite Elements Analysis
• Structural Inspections
• Structures Renewal Feasibility Studies
• On-site Works Supervision
• Scheme Management
Graduates will be expected to contribute to the design of structures from inception to completion, undertake the assessment of existing structures throughout the different stages such as on-site inspection and analysis, or manage the resources and tasks within a scheme of structures. AECOM is committed to the development of our graduates providing mobility between different projects and gradually increasing the level of responsibility within the firm.

Qualifications
• BEng in Civil or Structural Engineering, with a 2:1 classification (or equivalent) or above
• MEng or MSc in Civil or Structural Engineering would be an advantage
• Structural modules or Structural/Bridge Engineering experience would be an advantage
• Ability to demonstrate a good technical understanding of Civil & Structural Engineering
• Demonstrable interest in Bridge Structures Engineering and developing a career in this industry
• Willing and able to work towards chartership with the Institute of Civil Engineers (ICE) or Institute of Structural Engineers (ISructE)
• Good Microsoft Office skills essential such as Word, Excel & PowerPoint
• Ability to communicate effectively to internal and external clients, both verbally & in writing with the confidence to engage with a variety of people (clients, colleagues, stakeholders and sub-contractors alike) and the aptitude to rationally explain, explore and discuss technical issues and capture feedback
• Enthusiastic, hard-working, with ambition and drive
• Ability to structure & prioritise work effectively through close cooperation with the team as a whole
• Ability to work in a team and independently without losing initiative & focus.

Additional Information
• Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since CVs will be reviewed, and candidates selected on a rolling recruitment basis for either immediate or advanced offer start.
• Please include a covering letter with your application and provide all predicted and/or obtained academic grades and details of the dates you are able to work to/from and well as locations you would be interested in.
• You must have the right to work in the UK.
Professional Development
Our Graduate Development Programme (GDP), along with our huge scope of projects across the globe, will challenge and inspire you to make a real difference to the world we live in. Our GDP forms a core part of our business strategy globally, designed to develop the best talent across numerous disciplines to lead our business into the future.  We have over 750 graduates on our programmes across the UK & Ireland, from over 40 different disciplines, each and every one of them making a tangible difference to the environment we all live and work in.
We will provide you with all the tools and support you need to achieve your professional development ambitions, including Chartership with the relevant international professional institution – where we have graduates working towards over 30 professional institutions in the UK & Ireland. We will push you to achieve the highest standards and expect our graduates to pass their professional review first time. You will be assigned a mentor to support and guide your development and undertake regular training modules throughout the programme. There will be on-the-job technical development and classroom training where required, and the opportunity to work on live client projects, with significant multi-disciplinary exposure.
At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.
About AECOM
AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable leg

About This Job
The Risk Management Lead (RML) serves as the subject matter expert for risk management and central monitoring in AbbVie’s Risk-Based Quality Management (RBQM) model. The RML leads the strategic planning, implementation, and continuous improvement of risk management practices across global clinical trials, partnering closely with study teams and Central Monitoring colleagues to cultivate a proactive and sustainable risk-mitigation culture in support of high-quality study execution and regulatory compliance.
• Lead embedding and adoption of the end-to-end RBQM model within and across clinical study teams.
• Partner with cross-functional leads to develop and implement risk management strategies across therapeutic areas/programs.
• Facilitate Risk Assessment and Mitigation Planning (RAMP) meetings; prepare, review, and update RAMP documentation throughout the study lifecycle.
• Guide cross-functional teams in identifying critical data/processes, defining relevant Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), and establishing effective risk controls and response plans.
• Ensure alignment of risk discussions with study plans and global monitoring strategies.
• Coach and influence teams in risk mindset, methodology, and process maturity while fostering organizational capabilities.
• Analyze quality metrics/data and risk signals across study, regional, and site levels to drive continuous improvement and early intervention.
• Monitor risk mitigation execution, track issue trends, and ensure proper documentation, escalation, and communication of risks/issues.
• Support inspection readiness, audit response, and regulatory compliance, in collaboration with Clinical Process Compliance and Quality Assurance.
• Lead and contribute to RBQM process optimization, knowledge sharing, and best practice dissemination across studies and therapeutic areas.

Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, risk-based, or related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
• Extensive comprehensive experience in clinical operations, with proven expertise in risk management, RBQM, or quality management.
• Excellent working knowledge of risk management methodologies (including risk identification, assessment, mitigation, and documentation).
• Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams, senior management, and drive change management initiatives.
• Deep understanding of ICH/GCP, regulatory standards, and clinical trial processes.
• Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills; proficiency with data analysis/visualization tools.
• Exceptional communication, documentation, and interpersonal skills.
• Proven ability to lead in a dynamic global environment with complex, multi-jurisdictional studies.
• Mandatory hybrid model: 3 days onsite (Marlow)
Key Stakeholders: Clinical Site Management (CSM), Clinical Study Leadership (CSL), Strategic Clinical Operations, Therapeutic Area Medical Directors, Data Science, Compliance, Clinical Process Compliance, Quality Assurance, Vendor Management, and other cross-functional partners.

Analog Design Intern – CSS Audio
Location: Edinburgh, Scotland
Job Description
Analog Devices is seeking an Analog Design Intern to join our Consumer Audio design team in Edinburgh.
The successful candidate will join a collaborative team developing the next generation of high-performance mixed-signal audio solutions. Working alongside experienced analog, mixed-signal and digital design engineers, the intern will contribute to real IC development activities while developing practical experience in transistor-level design, modelling, simulation and verification.
Our audio products combine precision analog and mixed-signal circuits, data converters, Class-D amplification and power-management functions. This internship provides an opportunity to apply university knowledge to real silicon designs and to develop an understanding of the complete IC development process.
Responsibilities
• Conduct circuit architecture research and feasibility studies.
• Design, simulate and verify analog and mixed-signal IC blocks under the guidance of experienced engineers.
• Develop simulation testbenches and contribute to design verification across process, voltage and temperature conditions.
• Analyse circuit performance and understand key trade-offs involving noise, distortion, power consumption, silicon area and robustness.
• Work closely with layout engineers during physical implementation and review.
• Participate in technical and design reviews.
• Support integration and verification of circuit blocks within larger mixed-signal systems.
• Where appropriate, contribute to behavioural/system-level modelling and silicon evaluation activities.
Minimum Qualifications
• Currently pursuing a BEng, MEng, MSc or PhD in Electronic/Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics or a closely related discipline.
• Good understanding of analog circuit fundamentals and CMOS device operation.
• Familiarity with common analog building blocks such as amplifiers, comparators, references, bias circuits and oscillators.
• Understanding of feedback, frequency response and circuit stability.
• Some experience with circuit simulation and electronic design tools.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Good written and verbal communication skills.
• Ability and enthusiasm to work collaboratively within an engineering team.
Preferred Qualifications
• Familiarity with transistor-level IC design and Cadence Virtuoso/Spectre.
• Understanding of ADCs, DACs or delta-sigma conversion.
• Understanding of Class-D amplifiers or other audio signal-chain circuits.
• Familiarity with switched-mode power supplies such as buck, boost or charge-pump converters.
• Experience with MATLAB, Python or similar modelling/data-analysis tools.
• Experience using laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, signal generators and audio/precision measurement equipment.
• A genuine interest in analog IC design and a passion for audio.

The role works closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Operations and Programme, Project & Product Management, using a plan to prioritise and close open obsolescence issues.
Main Responsibilities:
• Own and maintain the company obsolescence-management process, governance, procedures, registers and Obsolescence Management Plans, aligned with contractual requirements and recognised good practice such as IEC 62402.
• Monitor bills of material, approved parts, materials for lifecycle risk using supplier notices, product change notifications, end-of-life notices, market intelligence and approved lifecycle tools.
• Maintain accurate ERP, PLM and obsolescence-system data attributing to role, including lifecycle status, affected products, risk ratings, owners, actions, due dates and supporting evidence.
• Assess the impact of each issue on safety, compliance, quality, configuration, cost, inventory, schedule, production continuity, product supportability and customer commitments.
• Coordinate cross-functional investigations and recommend proportionate mitigation, including authorised alternate sources, form-fit-function substitutes, last-time or lifetime buys, repair, redesign, technology refresh or controlled product phase-out.
• Assist preparation of robust business cases and technical recommendations, balancing lifecycle demand, total cost, lead time, minimum order quantities, storage life, qualification effort and residual risk.
• Work with Engineering, Quality and Programme Management to ensure replacement solutions are appropriately evaluated, qualified, approved and implemented through formal change control processes.
• Work with wider Supply Chain team to receive timely lifecycle information, validate notices, identify alternatives and improve the quality and timeliness of obsolescence data.
• Chair regular Obsolescence Review Meetings; communicate priorities, decisions, dependencies and escalations; and drive actions through to verified closure.
• Develop and report key performance indicators covering exposure, ageing, response time, mitigation status, cost avoidance, residual risk and data quality.
• Support new product introduction, sourcing and design reviews by promoting lifecycle-aware component selection, second-source strategies and long-term availability considerations in conjunction with wider Supply Chain team.
• Ensure proposed mitigations comply with applicable quality, regulatory, environmental, export-control, customer, counterfeit-avoidance and traceability requirements.
• Provide training, guidance and continuous improvement to embed proactive obsolescence ownership across relevant functions and perform other duties or special projects as assigned.
Education/ Qualifications:
• HNC/HND, degree or equivalent experience in electronic, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing or systems engineering, supply chain, or a related technical discipline.
• Professional qualification or formal training in obsolescence, component engineering, lifecycle management, configuration management or project management.
Knowledge and Experience:
• Experience of obsolescence, DMSMS, component engineering, product lifecycle, through-life support or technical supply-chain management.
• Knowledge of electronic, electromechanical or mechanical components and their lifecycle risks
• Experience interpreting bills of material, engineering drawings, specifications, supplier notices and lifecycle data.
• Understanding of ERP/MRP and PLM systems, configuration control and engineering change processes.
• Experience of risk assessment, technical investigations, mitigation planning and supplier engagement.
• Knowledge of IEC 62402, counterfeit avoidance, REACH, RoHS and aerospace or defence quality requirements.
Competencies:
• Strong analytical, data-management and problem-solving skills.
• IT literate, including advanced capability in Excel and confidence working with lifecycle databases and reporting tools.
• Able to evaluate technical and commercial options and make clear, evidence-based recommendations.
• Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, risks, actions and deadlines.
• Excellent written and verbal communication, stakeholder-management and influencing skills.
• Detail-oriented, proactive, resilient and able to work autonomously while coordinating cross-functional teams.
Other:
• SC cleared or ability to obtain.
• Ability to travel to company, supplier and customer locations as required.
• Flexibility to work additional hours when business-critical obsolescence events require urgent action.

Through a focus on continual improvement and operational excellence, the role will ensure BDO's Security Operations function remains proactive, effective and aligned to the organisation's evolving security needs.

Company Overview
At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.
Department Overview
The 'Pronto' team serves as the UK's leading provider of mobile policing applications, supporting 50% of the country's 45 police forces and over 70,000 active officers each day. The Hosted Applications team takes primary responsibility for managing the Pronto application across the hosted environment. Our dedicated group remotely oversees these Pronto instances for all hosted customers, directly ensuring platform stability, driving optimal performance, and maintaining continuous operational monitoring.
Job Description
This role is primarily remote, with occasional travel to offices.
Operating within Motorola Solutions’ Hosted Applications Team, the Systems Engineer holds a highly technical role combining application lifecycle engineering with client-facing responsibilities. Leveraging over 3 years of engineering expertise, you will share accountability for managing and sustaining the operational resilience of the mission-critical Pronto Digital Policing application for frontline emergency services and police forces.
In this position, you will assist with key deployment initiatives for standard product enhancements and customised client features. You will act as a technical link between software engineering and shared platform services teams while maintaining direct customer engagement. Key responsibilities involve assisting in analysing software issues, supporting patch rollouts and release cycles, and contributing customer feedback towards application enhancements.
Serving as a technical point of contact, you will support client-facing operations, help align infrastructure and application workflows, and participate in technical discussions during weekly meetings and service reviews. You will also monitor platform health and key performance metrics to help uphold strict Service Level Agreement (SLA) standards, working alongside project managers to resolve technical issues for customers.
You will help maintain SQL Server clusters, which house essential Pronto application data. You will support data security, system reliability, and standard operational processes aligned with the daily needs of our police and emergency service teams.
Key responsibilities of Systems Engineer:
•
Service Reviews & Client Engagement: Participate in regular customer service reviews and weekly meetings with key police force stakeholders to assist in presenting system performance, address operational concerns, and support customer satisfaction efforts.
•
SLA & Delivery Oversight: Assist in monitoring system performance against agreed contractual SLAs, supporting team efforts to minimise downtime and prevent service-impacting incidents.
•
Software Engineering Liaison: Act as an operational liaison for the core Pronto Software Engineering team. Help gather operational insights and support release management activities, including application hotfixes, feature rollouts, and platform deployments.
•
Shared Services Collaboration: Work closely with the internal Shared Services team to align application demands with technical specifications and assist in submitting change requests as needed.
•
Documentation: Contribute to and maintain customer-facing Interface Control Documents (ICDs), detailing technical specifications and protocols required for external system integration with the Pronto platform.
•
Problem & Incident Management: Support the incident management team in investigating and resolving system issues, helping implement effective solutions and preventative measures.
•
Continuous Learning & Knowledge Sharing: Engage in active knowledge sharing within the team, participating in peer learning and documenting technical workflows to support team development.
Basic Requirements
•
Experience: 3+ years of progressive experience in Systems Engineering, Infrastructure Engineering, or Hosted Application Operations within enterprise or public safety environments.
•
Security Clearance: Must be eligible for and maintain regional security vetting (e.g., UK NPPV Level 3 and SC Clearance for public safety cloud environments).
•
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, System Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
•
Driver's License: Must hold a valid driver's license and own a vehicle for travel to customer sites.
•
On-Call Support: Must be willing and available to participate in an on-call rotation to support mission-critical systems and emergency operational needs.
Technical requirements:
•
Architecture & System Lifecycle: Understanding of enterprise architecture principles, end-to-end system workflows, and standard software deployment lifecycle practices.
•
Cloud & Hosting Environments: Hands-on experience supporting hosted application environments across AWS, Azure, or Private Cloud infrastructure.
•
OS & Web Infrastructure: Practical experience administering Windows and Linux operating systems, along with working knowledge of web/application servers, SSL/TLS certificates.
•
Database Management: Practical capability in supporting, querying, and resolving operational issues within enterprise relational databases (such as SQL Server, Oracle, or PostgreSQL).
•
Automation & Scripting: Proficiency using Python, Bash, or PowerShell to assist with routine tasks, build basic automation scripts, and monitor application health.
•
Observability & Telemetry: Familiarity with maintaining and using enterprise monitoring tools (such as Grafana, Prometheus, or the TIG stack) to maintain visibility over system health.
•
Incident Resolution & Diagnostics: Strong problem-solving and diagnostic skills to troubleshoot system incidents and support root cause analysis.
•
Stakeholder Alignment & Communication: Effective communication skills to collaborate with cross-functional technical teams, convey technical updates clearly, and support client interactions.

A bit about us
Big ambitions. Personal investment. That’s Beyond the Ordinary.
Ready to start your career, learn by doing and see where your ambitions could take you? Welcome to the Audit School Leaver Apprenticeship at BDO.
The programme starts on Monday, 20th September 2027, for an organisation-wide induction (you need to be able to attend). For Edinburgh and Glasgow roles you will start on the 30th August 2027.
We’re the only UK mid-market organisation with more than £1bn in turnover and 8,000 people. Audit at BDO gives you the chance to get involved and build experience from day one. Our Audit teams work across specialist areas including Pension Audit, Public Sector, Not-for-Profit, Financial Services and Technology Risk Assurance, giving you the chance to learn how different organisations work from the inside out.
You’ll be trusted to contribute early, but you won’t be expected to know everything straight away. You’ll learn alongside experienced colleagues, build your confidence through practical experience and have people around you to answer questions and help you develop.
It’s a place to turn big ambitions into a career, with people personally invested in your growth from the start.
And a bit about Audit
Over four years, you’ll gain hands-on experience while working towards your ACA, CFAB or ICAS/Robert Gordan University qualification. You’ll learn through challenging Audit work, build relationships with clients and develop technical, personal and commercial skills as your experience grows.
Starting your career straight from school is a big step, so support is part of the experience too. You’ll join a trainee community, work towards your qualifications alongside your peers and learn from colleagues at different levels across the organisation.
Our early careers people talk about being trusted with client work earlier than they expected, while having supportive teams around them and feeling comfortable asking questions as they learn.
You’ll build your career foundations by doing the work, with the coaching and support to help your confidence grow. When you complete the programme, there’s a permanent role waiting for you.
As for you
You’re curious, resilient and ready to learn. You enjoy solving problems, thinking things through and getting involved.
You don’t need to arrive with all the answers. Bring your ambition and willingness to learn, and we’ll give you opportunities to build your experience, confidence and skills from there.
Join us in one of the following locations - Birmingham, Bristol, Cambridge, Edinburgh, Gatwick, Glasgow, Guildford, Ipswich, Leeds, Liverpool, London, Manchester, Nottingham, Reading and Southampton.
One thing to note: you’ll need to live within a commutable distance of the office you apply to. Relocation support is not provided, so please consider this carefully before applying. Time together in person matters – whether that’s in the office or with clients. It gives you more opportunities to learn from your team, build relationships and get the most from working together.

• GCSEs at grade 4 and above in Maths and English, or Scottish National 5 grade A-C. You’ll also need to provide evidence if successful
• Commitment to balance study and professional work
• The right to work in the UK (we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for these roles as they do not meet the current minimum salary requirements for sponsorship set by the Home Office. Applications from candidates who have their own legal right to work within the UK must cover the duration of their 4-year training contract and employment)
• For the roles based in Edinburgh or Glasgow you will need to be residing in Scotland
How the interview process will go
We want you to know what to expect, so here’s the typical process:
• Online application form.
• Online assessments.
• Video interview.
• Virtual assessment centre.
• Final interview in person.
We’ll keep you updated at each stage and share resources to help you prepare. And just so you know: we don’t use AI in any part of our candidate screening process. Every application is reviewed by a real person.
What you get in return
Our benefits are designed to support your life in and outside of work, with options including additional leave, gym membership and employee discounts, alongside pension, health and wellbeing support and a range of protection benefits.

£26,615 - £28,275 dependable on location.

Before you go
Starting your career is a big step. At BDO, you’ll get the chance to learn by doing, work with clients and build strong foundations for where you want to go next.
You’ll bring the big ambitions. You’ll have people around you investing in your learning, confidence and development from the start.

Job Title
Delivery Lead
Job Description
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
Your Team:
This role sits within the new Product Operations team, reporting into the Product Operations Lead, and is deployed onto specific high-priority initiatives as and when they arise, working alongside the Product Managers and Engineering Leads of every squad involved. You'll also work closely with the Product Governance Specialist and Product Partnership Manager where an initiative touches governance approval or third-party contracts, and you'll feed initiative-level status into the Product Operations Lead's wider portfolio reporting and forums such as the Product Development Monthly.
Your role in the Team’s Success:
This is a role for someone who thrives on the big, complex, cross-cutting initiatives that don't fit neatly inside a single squad or even a single domain - platform migrations, new product line launches, multi-quarter strategic programmes that touch several product areas at once. As Delivery Lead you will own the end-to-end delivery of these initiatives, orchestrating multiple Product Managers, Engineering Leads, and squads toward a single outcome. This is a role within a product-led organisation where we need people who are focused on outcomes, not just governance and milestones.
What you’ll do:
Cross-squad and cross-domain orchestration
• Own the end-to-end delivery plan for major initiatives that span multiple squads and/or multiple product domains, sequencing work across teams that don't normally plan together.  Support teams to carve deliverables/plans into manageable slices, making sure value can be found in each slice.
• Identify and actively manage dependencies between squads and domains - the handoffs, shared components, and sequencing constraints that a single squad's Product Manager can't see or resolve alone.
• Bring together the right Product Managers, Engineering Leads, and other stakeholders at the right moments, without taking over their squads' day-to-day delivery.  Help to foster a psychologically safe working environment where people can raise problems, solve issues and find solutions.
Programme-level risk and issue management
• Maintain a single, honest view of risk, issues, and critical-path dependencies across the whole initiative, escalating early and clearly to the Product Operations Lead and senior stakeholders.
• Resolve conflicts where squads have competing priorities or constrained shared resources, making trade-offs visible rather than letting them cause silent slippage.
• Own contingency and mitigation planning for the risks that could derail a multi-team initiative — not just track them on a log.
Stakeholder alignment and communication
• Act as the single point of accountability for "how is this initiative actually going" — able to give senior stakeholders, up to and including the Product Development Monthly forum, a clear and credible answer at any point.
• Keep Product Managers, Engineering Leads, and other functions (Compliance, Legal, Data) aligned to a shared plan and timeline, even when their day-to-day priorities pull in different directions.
• Translate initiative complexity into simple, decision-ready updates for senior leadership.
Technical and delivery credibility
• Bring a high level of technical fluency to understand system dependencies, integration points, and engineering trade-offs across multiple domains.
• Apply sound programme and project management discipline (planning, milestone tracking, RAID management) appropriate to initiatives that are often unprecedented and don't fit a standard template.
Contribution to Product Operations
• Feed lessons learned and delivery best practice back into the Product Operations Lead, helping the wider team get better at running complex, cross-cutting initiatives.
• Support the Product Operations Lead with ad hoc portfolio-level analysis or reporting when capacity allows between initiatives.
What You'll Need:
• Significant experience as a Programme Manager, Senior Delivery Manager, or Technical Project Manager, with a track record of delivering initiatives that span multiple teams or workstreams.
• Demonstrable experience managing complex cross-team dependencies and driving them to resolution, not just tracking them.
• Strong stakeholder management skills, including the credibility and gravitas to align Product Managers and Engineering Leads who don't report into you.
• Enough technical understanding to engage credibly with engineering leaders on architecture, sequencing, and trade-offs across multiple systems or domains.
• Excellent communication skills — able to distil a genuinely complex, multi-team initiative into a clear, honest update for senior leadership.
• Comfortable with ambiguity — these initiatives often don't have a standard playbook, and you'll need to build the plan as much as follow one.
• Open to ambiguity - people need a plan, but they we expect you to be dynamic and adaptable when circumstances inevitably change.
Desirable
• Experience in a regulated financial services or fintech environment.
• Direct experience delivering platform migrations, re-platforming, or major organisational/domain restructuring initiatives.
• Programme or project management qualifications (e.g. MSP, PMP, Prince2) — useful context, though real-world judgement on ambiguous, high-stakes initiatives matters more.
• Deep experience of agile ways of working, to work effectively with Product Managers and Engineering Leads running their own ceremonies and backlogs.
The Perks
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.
• Competitive salary

• Private medical cover for you and your family
• Life insurance

• Maintain oversight of vessel certification and statutory compliance.

• Support crew competence development, including familiarization and drills.
• Review crew matrix and support compliance with terminal and charterer requirements.
Documentation & Continuous Improvement:
• Review and update company procedures based on operational feedback.
• Ensure effective use of digital tools (e.g.,  Mariapps, ERBs).
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives across fleet operations and HSEQ  performance.
Emergency Response:

• Provide support during incidents and emergencies.

• Relevant training in LNG or Tanker operations
• ISM/ISO Lead Auditor certification will be an advantage.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
• Effective communication skills (written and verbal).

Author and revise SOPs, technical protocols, and reports while identifying opportunities to improve laboratory workflows, analytical reliability, and stability program execution.

Be extraordinary at AWE.
About the apprenticeship
Engineering-related disciplines are at the heart of AWE, helping us maintain and develop the facilities, equipment and systems that support our mission to keep the nation safe and secure.
As a Level 3 Engineering Apprentice, you’ll apply through a single Engineering Apprenticeship route. During the selection process, we’ll take time to understand your interests, strengths and aspirations to help identify the engineering pathway that best suits you and aligns with business needs.
Throughout the selection process, you’ll have the opportunity to learn more about our different engineering specialisms, meet members of the teams and ask questions about the pathways available. This will help us work together to determine the area that offers the best fit for your skills, potential and future development.
From the start of your apprenticeship, you will be aligned to your specific engineering pathway, giving you the opportunity to develop practical skills, technical knowledge and industry experience within your specialist area. Through a combination of hands-on training and college study, you’ll build the foundations needed for a successful career.

The pathway you follow will shape the type of engineering work you learn and the skills you develop. You do not need to know everything about each area before you apply — the selection process will help you learn more about the options and identify where your interests, strengths and potential may fit best.
Mechanical Maintenance
You’ll work hands-on with machinery and mechanical equipment, helping to find and fix faults, replace parts, and keep facilities and equipment running safely and reliably.
Electrical Maintenance
You’ll work with electrical equipment, wiring and systems, helping to install, test, maintain and repair the technology that powers our facilities and equipment.
Control & Instrumentation (C&I) Maintenance
You’ll work with the sensors, instruments and control systems that help monitor and control temperature, pressure, flow and system performance, making sure equipment works as it should.
Precision Machining
You’ll use specialist machines, drawings and measuring tools to make accurate components to the right shape, size and finish, developing precision, attention to detail and practical manufacturing skills.
Mechatronic Maintenance
You’ll work with mechanical, electrical and automated systems, helping to maintain advanced equipment and understand how different engineering areas work together.
Opportunities when you complete your apprenticeship
Following successful completion of your apprenticeship, and subject to business need and your career aspirations, you’ll move into a role within the business, aligned to the pathway you have trained in.
Whatever pathway you follow, you’ll become part of a skilled community, supporting some of the UK’s most unique facilities, equipment, processes and technologies, while continuing to develop your career at AWE.

We are seeking a reliable and safety-conscious Class 2 HGV Driver to join our team based at Furzebrook.
In this role, you will be responsible for operating a Class 2 LGV rigid tipper vehicle, transporting quarry materials safely and efficiently between the production face, processing plant, storage facilities, and customer delivery locations. The majority of your work will involve moving material from the quarry to designated tipping bays for processing, with occasional deliveries to dockside and storage facilities at Poole Quay to support shipping operations.

• Conduct comprehensive pre-use vehicle inspections at the start of every shift, identifying and reporting any defects immediately and taking appropriate action to ensure the vehicle remains safe and roadworthy.
• Transport pit grades from the quarry to the processing site, tipping material into designated bays for processing. When required, transport material directly from the quarry to dockside facilities or covered storage at Poole Quay to support shipping operations.
• Ensure full compliance with all Road Transport Regulations, including Drivers' Hours, Working Time Directive requirements, and Tachograph regulations, maintaining minimal infringements.
• Download and submit Digital Tachograph Driver Card data on a weekly basis in line with company requirements.
• Attend and maintain Driver CPC training, ensuring the required 35 hours of periodic training is completed within each five-year cycle and keeping all qualifications up to date.
• Maintain the vehicle to a high standard by regularly cleaning external areas, the tipper body, and removing any retained material where necessary.
• Keep the vehicle cab clean, tidy, and presentable at all times.
• Take responsibility for ensuring the vehicle is in a fit, safe, and roadworthy condition before and during operation.
• Adhere to all company procedures, site rules, speed limits, and prevailing road or site conditions, operating the vehicle in a safe and professional manner.
• Report any changes to driving licence status, endorsements, or other relevant driving-related information promptly.
• Accurately complete all required documentation, vehicle records, and compliance paperwork as required.
• Represent the company professionally when interacting with customers, site personnel, contractors, and members of the public.

Essential Qualifications
• Valid Class 2 HGV (Category C) Driving Licence.
• Valid Driver CPC Qualification Card.
• GCSEs (or equivalent) in English and Math.
Essential Skills & Experience
• Minimum of 1 year experience driving HGV Class 2 vehicles.
• Strong understanding of Drivers' Hours Regulations, Tachographs, and the Working Time Directive.
• Commitment to maintaining high standards of health and safety.
• Good communication skills and the ability to work independently.
Desirable Experience
• Previous tipper vehicle driving experience.
• Experience working within a quarrying, aggregates, mining, or construction environment.
• Knowledge of quarry safety procedures and site operations.

Director of Clinical Services
The Alexandra Hospital
37.5 Hours & Permanent
The Alexandra Hospital in Cheadle Is part of Circle Health Group, Britain's leading provider of independent healthcare with a nationwide network of hospitals & clinics, performing more complex surgery than any other private healthcare provider in the country.
The Alexandra is one of the UK's leading private hospitals and a major centre for complex and advanced healthcare outside the M25.
We have an exceptional opportunity for an outstanding Director of Clinical Services to join our Senior Management Team at The Alexandra Hospital.
This pivotal role will provide strategic and professional leadership across the hospital's clinical services, shaping clinical strategy, strengthening standards of care and ensuring the continued delivery of safe, effective and consistently excellent outcomes for every patient.
As a key member of the hospital's senior leadership team, you will help shape its future direction, aligning clinical services with organisational priorities while driving operational excellence, developing our workforce and fostering a culture of continuous improvement, innovation and accountability.
We are looking for an exceptional nurse leader who can inspire confidence, bring people together around a shared vision and make a lasting contribution to the hospital's strategy, culture and performance.
Duties of this role include:
• Lead the clinical governance agenda, ensuring compliance with all regulatory, legal and professional standards, maintaining a minimum CQC rating of GOOD while striving for OUTSTANDING.
• Provide visible clinical leadership and clinical on-call support, acting as the senior advisor on all clinical matters across the hospital.
• Ensure all necessary measures are taken to safeguard the health, safety and wellbeing of patients, maintaining a high-quality, safe clinical environment.
• Maintain and uphold professional standards in line with NMC, HCPC, GMC and other relevant regulatory bodies.
• Ensure safe staffing levels across all clinical areas, with appropriate skill mix, staff competency and workforce development at all times.
• Lead hospital participation in internal and external audits, ensuring timely completion of actions, compliance with requirements and adherence to best practice.
• Drive quality improvement, patient safety initiatives and effective risk management, ensuring learning from incidents, investigations and audits is embedded into clinical practice.
• Strengthen multidisciplinary collaboration, building trust and effective working relationships across clinical and operational teams to improve service delivery and patient outcomes.
• Influence effectively at executive level, translating strategic priorities into consistently excellent clinical practice and ensuring clinical services support the hospital's wider organisational objectives.
• Maintain a strong focus on operational performance, responding effectively to changing market conditions and service demands while identifying opportunities for innovation and service development.
• Champion professional standards, staff engagement and continuous improvement, ensuring patient safety, workforce development and clinical quality remain central to decision-making.
• Lead investigations, audits and risk management activities, ensuring learning is embedded, appropriate actions are implemented and clinical practice continues to improve.
• Play a leading role in shaping the hospital's future direction, strengthening its reputation for excellence and making a lasting contribution to its strategy, culture and performance.
Applicants should meet the following criteria:
• Be a Registered Nurse with current RCN registration.
• Bring extensive senior clinical leadership experience, including substantial experience within private healthcare.
• A critical care background would be advantageous.
• Previous NHS clinical experience would be desirable.
• Demonstrate a strong understanding of complex healthcare environments, clinical governance, risk management, operational service delivery and multidisciplinary working.
• Have a proven track record of success in clinical governance, risk management and quality improvement, driving improvements in clinical standards and patient outcomes.
• Possess a thorough understanding of regulatory and professional standards, including CQC, NICE, NMC and HCPC requirements, alongside relevant national healthcare frameworks.
• Demonstrate excellent leadership, communication and change management skills, with the ability to influence at executive level and lead teams through change effectively.
• Have proven experience leading investigations, managing clinical risk and embedding learning from incidents, audits and reviews to support continuous improvement.
• Be an authentic, visible and credible nurse leader who builds trust, leads with integrity and emotional intelligence, and engages and develops high-performing teams.
• Demonstrate strong strategic thinking and the ability to translate organisational priorities into consistently excellent clinical practice.
• Have experience balancing clinical quality, workforce development and operational performance while responding effectively to changing service demands.

Circle Health Group is committed to offering competitive starting salaries and access to a wide range of employee benefits, including:

• Private Healthcare Scheme for treatment at our hospitals, covering pre-existing medical conditions

• Family Friendly policies, including enhanced Maternity, Paternity & Adoption pay
• Non-contributory life insurance

…and much more!

Registered Veterinary Nurse
Salary: Circa £30,000 DOE
Location: City Vets, Heavitree, Exeter
Job Type: Permanent
Looking for more than “just nursing”?
If you’re an RVN looking for a role where you can develop your clinical skills, gain excellent exposure to a busy main centre and become part of a highly supportive nursing team, this could be the opportunity you’ve been looking for.
At City Vets, our nursing team is at the heart of what we do. We are a progressive, ambitious team who give our nurses the opportunity to take on responsibility, develop their interests and get involved in a much broader range of clinical work than traditional nursing duties.
Our main centre in Heavitree is an RCVS-accredited practice, supported by three nearby branch practices in Alphington, St Thomas and Whipton. Across the group, you’ll have exposure to a large and varied caseload, modern equipment and a team of experienced colleagues who genuinely want to help you progress.
Why City Vets is different for nurses
This is a role where you’ll get excellent exposure to a busy, varied clinical environment.
You’ll work alongside a supportive team of 12 vets, 9 RVNs and dedicated support staff, with experienced lead nurses available to guide and mentor you. For a newly qualified RVN, or someone looking to develop their skills within a busy main centre, this provides the perfect balance of support and opportunity.
Our nurses are trusted to do far more than traditional day-to-day nursing duties. You’ll have opportunities to develop your skills in:
• Stage 1 dental procedures
• Nurse-led outpatient CT
• Advanced imaging and patient preparation
• Anaesthesia and inpatient care
• Dental imaging and procedures
• Nurse-led consultations
• Minor procedures, including lump removals
• Supporting complex and interesting cases
• Exotic patient care
We also have dedicated dentistry expertise within the practice, alongside CT, ultrasound, digital radiography, endoscopy and dental imaging. Our separate wards for dogs, cats and exotics mean you’ll gain exposure to a broad range of patients and clinical presentations.
Interested in exotics? Even better.
If you have an interest in exotic nursing, there is plenty here to get excited about.
We see a varied exotic caseload and have nurses with experience and further qualifications in exotics. You’ll have the opportunity to build your knowledge and confidence with exotic patients while working alongside colleagues who are happy to share their experience.
Our practices are also proud to hold Cat Friendly Clinic accreditation through the ISFM, while St Thomas holds Silver Rabbit Friendly accreditation through the RWAF and Heavitree is a Gold Standard RWAF practice.
A team that wants you to progress
We believe that being supported doesn’t mean being held back.
Our nursing team is structured to give you access to experienced lead nurses and Clinical Nursing Managers, with clear opportunities to develop your skills and progress internally. If there’s an area of nursing you’re passionate about, we want to help you explore it.
Whether your interests lie in dentistry, imaging, anaesthesia, exotics, inpatient care or consultations, we’ll support you to develop your career in the direction that suits you.
We already have multiple nursing certificate holders across exotics, anaesthesia, imaging and dentistry, and we actively support our team with further qualifications and CPD. We offer extensive internal and funded external CPD because we believe investing in our nurses ultimately means better care for our patients.
Great facilities. Great caseload. Even better support.
Our Heavitree main centre is extremely well equipped, with:
• CT scanner
• Ultrasound
• Digital radiography
• Endoscopy
• Dental imaging
• Separate wards for dogs, cats and exotics
• Dedicated dentistry facilities
We also benefit from certificate holders across the wider veterinary team, visiting specialists in cardiology, ophthalmology and physiotherapy, regular CPD events and dedicated input from Cave Veterinary Specialists. We work closely with local referral hospitals, giving our team excellent clinical support when cases require it.
Your wellbeing matters too
We want you to build a rewarding career without sacrificing your life outside work.
Our out-of-hours service is outsourced, helping to protect work-life balance, while inpatient care remains in-house during our normal working arrangements. Weekend duties are shared fairly across the veterinary team.
And then there’s Exeter itself  with the coast, estuary, moors and countryside on your doorstep, alongside a vibrant food scene and excellent transport links to London and beyond.
What we’re looking for
We’re looking for an RVN who is:
• Motivated and keen to develop clinically
• Passionate about delivering excellent patient care
• Confident or keen to develop as a consulting nurse
• Interested in learning from a varied and interesting caseload
• A strong team player who enjoys working collaboratively
• Committed to providing an excellent client experience
• Interested in developing additional clinical skills
• Interested in exotics advantageous, but not essential
Whether you’re newly qualified and looking for the right environment to build your confidence, or an experienced RVN looking for greater responsibility and progression, we’d love to hear from you.
What we offer
• Circa £30,000 salary, depending on experience
• 5 weeks’ holiday plus bank holidays and birthday leave
• Relocation support
• RCVS and VDS fees paid
• Employer contribution pension scheme
• Generous staff discount scheme
• Life assurance
• E-car salary sacrifice scheme
• Enhanced equal family leave
• Extensive internal and funded external CPD
• Genuine opportunities for clinical development and progression
Ready to take your nursing career further?
If you’re looking for a role where your skills will be valued, your development will be supported and you’ll have the opportunity to do more, City Vets could be the right fit for you.
Come and join a nursing team where nurses really are our superpower.

Job Description Summary
#LI-Hybrid
Internal job title: Director
Location: London, UK
The Director, Translational Medicine Expert (Neurodegeneration) will lead the end to end translational strategy for neurodegenerative programs, bridging preclinical research to early clinical development (Phase 1–2).
This role is accountable for biomarker strategy, clinical endpoint selection, and early phase trial design, enabling efficient, data driven decision-making through key development milestones (e.g., Transition Decision Points) and ensuring competitive differentiation of neuromuscular assets.
In addition, he/she oversees the planning, execution, and interpretation of clinical trials research, data collection activities and clinical operations. Establishes and approves scientific methods for design and implementation of clinical protocols, data collection systems and final reports. Support new and ongoing clinical research and clinical trials and ensure efficient and timely processing of confidentiality agreements and clinical agreements
Job Description
Key Responsibilities:
1. Translational Strategy & Program Leadership
•
• Define and execute integrated translational strategies across neurodegeneration programs
• Lead translational components from preclinical → Phase 1/2 clinical studies
• Drive program progression through key decision gates (e.g., IND, TDP, IDPA)
• Ensure strong mechanistic linkage between target biology, biomarkers, and clinical endpoints
2. Biomarker & Endpoint Leadership
•
• Collaborate with Biomarker Development colleagues toward development and validation of:
• Molecular biomarkers (tissue, blood, CSF where applicable)
• Functional endpoints (strength, mobility, disease-specific measures)
• Patient-reported outcomes (PROs)
• Establishing quantitative biomarkers to support:
• Target engagement
• Disease modification
• Dose selection and PoC decisions
• Integrate biomarker strategy into clinical protocols and operational plans
• Drive early biomarker de‑risking, a key priority in neuromuscular programs
3. Early Clinical Development (Phase 1/2)
•
• Co‑lead design and execution of early clinical studies
• Define:
• Dose escalation strategy
• Exposure–response framework
• Translational endpoints (biopsy, imaging, functional)
• Ensure TM leadership within Clinical Trial Teams (CTTs) for:
• Trial design
• Execution oversight
• Data interpretation and decision-making
4. Cross-Functional Leadership
•
• Serve as core Translational Medicine representative within global project teams
• Partner closely with:
• Clinical Development
• Biomarker Development
• Clinical Pharmacology (PKS)
• Preclinical Safety (PCS)
• Regulatory
• Drive alignment between research, TM, and development organizations
5. External Scientific Leadership
•
• Build and lead collaborations with:
• Academic KOLs
• Patient advocacy groups (critical in rare neuromuscular disease)
• Technology partners (imaging, omics platforms)
• Contribute to scientific strategy and external positioning of programs
6. Patient-Centered Development
•
• Integrate the patient voice into translational and clinical strategies
• Advance:
• Meaningful functional endpoints
• Patient-relevant outcome measures
• Innovative trial approaches (e.g., decentralized models where feasible)
7. Portfolio Contribution & Strategic Input
•
• Contribute to:
• Asset prioritization and portfolio strategy
• Competitive differentiation strategy (e.g., vs RNA or gene therapy competitors)
• Provide scientific input to:
• Business development / due diligence
• Indication expansion strategies
Essential Requirements:
·       MD, neurologists, clinical training in neurodegenerative diseases
·       Experience in translational medicine, early clinical development, or experimental therapeutics.
·       Ability to shape development strategies, execute early clinical studies, and influence regulatory/packages supporting differentiation.

·       Experience working in pharmaceutical/biotech company strongly preferred.
·       PhD, PharmD, or equivalent in:
o   Neurology / Neuroscience
o   Neurodegenerative diseases
